datasets.title: Flood Impact Assessment in North Taungoo, Bago State, Myanmar as of 02 October 2024
datasets.description: UNOSAT code: FL20240912MMR This map illustrates satellite detected floods using WorldView-3 images acquired on 02 October 2024. Within the analysed area of about 23 km², a total of about 21 km² of land appears to be affected by flood waters with about 18 km² of cropland inundated. UNITAR-UNOSAT identified approximately 2,240 affected buildings, representing 94% of the buildings as well as 35 km of affected roads, covering 88% of the roads in the analysed area. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to the United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/flood-impact-assessment-in-north-taungoo-bago-state-myanmar-as-of-02-october-2024]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts processed WorldView-3 satellite imagery acquired on 02 October 2024 over North Taungoo, Bago State, Myanmar, comparing pre- and post-flood images to delineate flood extent and identify affected assets. Satellite-detected inundation polygons were intersected with building footprints, cropland, and road networks to quantify direct impacts. This preliminary post-event damage assessment provides empirical flood hazard extent and direct loss estimates for buildings, agriculture, and infrastructure.
